title: 第1章 天煞孤星
slug: 花千骨全本免费-花千骨最新章节列表
content_zh:
“南无阿弥陀佛南无阿弥陀佛……”一个约莫十二三岁的小孩孤零零一个人在路上急速的走着。右手握着一小串佛珠碎碎的念，左手提着个油皮灯笼。
与其说她是走不如说是在跑，因为那些东西一直在后面跟着她，只是因为佛珠的原因不敢太靠近。周围漆黑一片，只看得见灯笼荧荧鬼火一般在半空中飘移着。四野寂静得有些诡异，连流水声，虫鸣声都听不见。
马上就要到村子里了，进了村就好了，小孩不断提醒自己，苍白着脸，冷汗直往下掉。腾出右手把身上披的八只黑狗皮拼制成的披风裹得更严实一点，妄图不让自己的气味更多的散发出去。
可是走到村头的小石拱桥上，小孩还是傻那里了。一个打着纸伞的女人站在桥上正对着她，伞面上绣的是红得耀眼的桃花，白色的衣裙上也是。伞打得很低，看不见脸。明明是炎热酷闷得没有一点风，可是那裙袂却激荡的上下翻飞着。
小孩吓得停在那里双腿直打颤，完了，遇上鬼拦路了。
“南无阿弥陀佛……”她继续低声念着，侧过身子想从桥另一边过，低下头装作没看见她。却发现她眨眼间又站在了她的面前。精致的白色绣花鞋上沾满了泥，脚边是一滩的水，还有各种绿色的水藻和贝壳。这时她才看清，那裙摆上的哪是桃花，分明是溅染的鲜血。
突然，手中灯笼本应该温柔的黄光开始诡异的从青色变成红色，好像也被血染过了一样。空气里满是刺鼻的河里的膻气与血的腥臭。
“南无阿弥陀佛……”硬着头皮把佛珠举到前面，那女鬼退了两步，小孩又前进两步，那女鬼又退两步。快到桥头时，却听一阵令人毛骨悚然的笑声响起。
咣的一下，面前的女鬼散裂了开来，肢体断作无数截，仿佛被硬生生砍碎一样，一地都是血和蛆虫。
小孩吓得差点扔了手中的佛珠还有灯笼就往回跑，两条腿抖个不行。
却见有个圆圆的东西骨碌碌的从伞下滚了出来，滚缠着黑色的长发，竟然是那个女人的头。小孩浑身上下如被冰冻，半点都动不了了。一个声音不停的在心底喊，快跑快跑，可就是挪不开半步。
那头皮球一般，S型的左右乱窜，撞到桥栏又反弹回来，一会儿就蹭到了小孩的脚边，吓得她差点没整个瘫软的坐在地上。
静止了片刻，小孩瞪着脚边那个突然不动的头，心都快从喉咙里跳出来。却见突然，那个头一下翻转过来，小孩这才看到她的脸，脸上黑乎乎的两个大洞，眼睛竟然被硬生生抠去。一只不知道到哪里去了，另一只由一些血管、神经和组织牵连着半挂在脸上，晃来晃去，白惨惨的眼珠还飞快的转着，向上直瞪着她。嘴唇似是被河里的鱼都咬烂了，残缺不全得瑟瑟哆嗦似是要向她说些什么，却只发出风吹木头门一样嘎嘎的响声。
小孩忍住呕吐的冲动，跨过那个头就往前跑，顾不得正踩在一地的残肢上。突然间腿被抓住，是一只半截的右手，手指在水里泡涨了，腐烂而发白，手臂肉端处可以看见森森的白骨。
惊恐当中，发现那个脑袋又飞快的向自己弹了过来，张开大嘴就咬到了自己的右腿小腿上，剧痛之中更加伴随的是刺骨的阴冷，瞬间传遍了四肢百骸。
小孩挥舞着佛珠向那头上打去，然后听见一阵仿佛生肉放在烧红铁板上的嘶嘶响声，好一半天那个头才松口脱落。小孩拔腿就跑，却突然听见什么破裂的声音，脚底下什么东西硌着自己。抬起来一看，竟然是那女鬼的另一只眼球不小心被自己踩爆了，正流出滚滚的脓水和蛆虫。
小孩一边干呕一边飞也似的逃下桥，发现那只手竟然还抓在自己腿上，而那个脑袋还在桥上蹦呀蹦呀，上下牙齿互相敲打着，叫着“手，手，手……”声音又凄惨又恐怖，只是下不了桥，无法追来。惨死在水上的人，灵魂只能永远困在那里。
小孩使劲把那残臂从腿上扯了下来，用力的抛回桥上。然后转身不要命的往前跑。脸上早吓得半点血色都没有了。
村子里的人此时都睡了，安静得连声鸡鸣狗叫都听不到。小孩在一家药店前疯狂敲门，整村人却仿佛都在睡梦中死去一样，没有半点反应，没有一家灯亮。小孩拼着命的敲了好半天里面才有了一点动静。

content_en:
"Namo Amitabha, Namo Amitabha..." A child of about twelve or thirteen years old was walking quickly on the road alone. In her right hand, she held a small string of Buddhist beads and chanted them in pieces, while in her left hand, she held an oil-skin lantern.
She was running rather than walking, because those things had been following her, but they didn't dare to get too close because of the beads. It was pitch dark all around, and only lanterns could be seen drifting in the air like will-o'-the-wisps. The surrounding fields were eerily quiet, not even the sound of running water or the chirping of insects could be heard.
We are about to arrive at the village. It will be fine once we enter the village. The child kept reminding himself, with a pale face and cold sweat falling down. He freed up his right hand to wrap the cloak made of eight black dog skins around him more tightly, in an attempt to prevent his scent from spreading.
But when they reached the small stone arch bridge at the end of the village, the child was still confused. A woman holding a paper umbrella stood facing her on the bridge. The umbrella was embroidered with dazzling red peach blossoms, and the white dress was also embroidered. The umbrella was held so low that I couldn't see my face. It was obviously hot and stuffy with no wind at all, but the skirt was flying up and down in excitement.
The child was so frightened that he stopped there and his legs were shaking. It was over, and a ghost was blocking his way.
"Namo Amitabha..." She continued to mutter in a low voice, turning sideways to cross the other side of the bridge, lowering her head and pretending not to see her. Only to find that she was standing in front of her again in the blink of an eye. The delicate white embroidered shoes were covered with mud, and there was a puddle of water beside her feet, as well as various green algae and shells. Only then did she see clearly that the peach blossoms on the skirt were clearly splattered with blood.
Suddenly, the gentle yellow light of the lantern in his hand began to strangely change from cyan to red, as if it had been stained by blood. The air was filled with the pungent smell of the river and the stench of blood.
"Namo Amitabha..." He bravely raised the beads to the front. The female ghost took two steps back, the child took two steps forward, and the female ghost took two steps back. As they approached the bridge, they heard a creepy laughter.
With a bang, the female ghost in front of her fell apart. Her limbs were broken into countless pieces, as if she had been chopped into pieces. The ground was covered with blood and maggots.
The child was so frightened that he almost threw away the prayer beads and lantern in his hand and ran back, his legs shaking.
But he saw something round and round rolling out from under the umbrella, with long black hair wrapped around it. It turned out to be the woman's head. The child's whole body felt like it was frozen and he couldn't move at all. A voice kept shouting in my heart, run, run, but I couldn't move even half a step.
The ball was like a ball, S-shaped, scurrying left and right, hitting the bridge railing and then bouncing back. After a while, it touched the child's feet, scaring her so much that she almost collapsed and sat on the ground.
After being still for a moment, the child stared at the suddenly motionless head at his feet, his heart almost jumping out of his throat. Suddenly, the head turned over, and the child saw her face. There were two big black holes on her face, and her eyes had been gouged out. One of them had gone somewhere, and the other was half-hanging on her face, connected by some blood vessels, nerves and tissues, dangling back and forth. Its pale eyes were still turning rapidly, staring up at her. The lips seemed to have been bitten by the fish in the river, and they were so mutilated that they trembled as if they were about to say something to her, but they only made a rattling sound like the wind blowing on a wooden door.
The child resisted the urge to vomit, stepped over the head and ran forward, not caring that he was stepping on the stumps on the ground. Suddenly the leg was grabbed, and it was a half-cut right hand. The fingers were swollen in the water, rotting and turning white. Dense white bones could be seen at the end of the arm.
In the midst of panic, he found that the head quickly bounced towards him again, opened his big mouth and bit his right calf. The severe pain was accompanied by a biting coldness, which instantly spread throughout his limbs and bones.
The child waved his prayer beads and hit the head, and then heard a sound that sounded like raw meat being placed on the head.There was a hissing sound on the red-hot iron plate, and it took a long time before the head let go and fell off. The child ran away, but suddenly he heard a cracking sound and something struck him under his feet. When he raised it up, he saw that the female ghost's other eyeball had been accidentally stepped on by him, and it was leaking out boiling pus and maggots.
The child retched while running away from the bridge, and found that the hand was still holding on to his leg, and the head was still jumping on the bridge, his upper and lower teeth were beating against each other, shouting "Hand, hand, hand..." The sound was miserable and terrifying, but he couldn't get off the bridge and couldn't catch up. The souls of people who died tragically on the water can only be trapped there forever.
The child tore the residual arm from his leg and threw it back onto the bridge. Then he turned around and ran forward desperately. His face was so frightened that there was no color left at all.
Everyone in the village was asleep at this time, and it was so quiet that you couldn't even hear the crowing of chickens and the barking of dogs. A child knocked on the door frantically in front of a pharmacy, but the whole village seemed to have died in their sleep. There was no response and no lights were on. The child knocked hard for a long time before there was any movement inside.
